title: INPP
shortDescription: Movement-based programs addressing retained primitive reflexes and neuromotor immaturity.
description:
INPP stands for the Institute for Neuro-Physiological Psychology, founded in Chester, England in 1975. The INPP method is built on the idea of neuromotor immaturity — that some children retain early infant reflexes past the age they normally integrate, and that this can affect balance, coordination, handwriting, attention, and sensory processing.

An INPP assessment looks at gross and fine motor coordination, balance, eye movements, and the presence of retained primitive reflexes. If the assessment finds neuromotor immaturity, the practitioner prescribes a daily movement program — usually a small set of slow, specific exercises done at home for a few minutes a day, adjusted over months as the child progresses.

A note on evidence, because it matters when you are choosing where to spend limited time and money: INPP has a smaller and less rigorous research base than established autism therapies such as speech therapy, occupational therapy, or ABA. Some families report meaningful gains in coordination and attention; the primitive reflex model itself is not broadly accepted in mainstream pediatric neurology. Treat it as a complement to evidence-based services rather than a replacement for them, and talk it through with your child's pediatrician or developmental specialist before committing.

In Florida, INPP-trained practitioners are uncommon, and the programs are frequently offered by occupational therapists or educational specialists who have taken INPP training rather than by dedicated INPP clinics. Coverage is rarely available through insurance, so expect to ask about private-pay rates.
benefits: Home-based daily program requiring only a few minutes a day

May support handwriting, attention, and sensory regulation
Parents deliver the program, so no daily clinic visits
